sentences.text: Seeleyosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur found in Germany and possibly Russia.
This animal was a relatively small plesiosaur measuring between 2.88 and 3.66 meters long and weighing 199 kilograms.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a large, almost complete skeleton discovered in the Upper Lias formations of Württemberg, Germany.
This original skeleton was purchased by the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart in August 1893.
Unfortunately, the original holotype skeleton was destroyed in 1945.
A second specimen was discovered in November 1906 by fossil trader Bernhard Hauff.
This second find intersected a forty-centimeter-thick layer of Stinkstein chalk in a quarry between Holzmaden and Zell unter Aichelberg.
A fragmentary specimen of Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris was identified from the Middle Jurassic of Siberia by Menner in 1992.
Seeleyosaurus was first described as Plesiosaurus guilelmiimperatoris by Dames in 1895 before being moved to its own genus by White in 1940.
The genus is classified within the family Microcleididae.
A 2025 study by Sachs et al. interpreted Plesiopterys wildi as a distinct taxon from Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris.
Seeleyosaurus lived during the Toarcian stage, approximately 184.2 to 182.9 million years ago.
